digest.component_or_area: comment hygiene detector and CI guard
propositions: Source code comments contain rot-prone historical references (commit SHAs, run/thread IDs, dated incident narratives) that become unresolvable over time due to rebasing and retention policies.
The newly implemented comment-hygiene detector scans code blocks for SHA-like hex (≥7 chars), run/job/thread IDs (≥8 digits), and date+incident-verb patterns to identify violating comments.

Detector acceptor must recognize ticket/epic/story/bug/rec/ADR IDs (4x4 hex-grouped or word-triple aliases) and the 'context: external' escape hatch as valid remediation, while rejecting false positives like 'bug surfaced' and path-embedded aliases.

All detector-hit sites must be remediated by one of three sanctioned forms: citing a resolvable ticket ID, dropping the rot-prone token while preserving durable prose, or replacing SHA narratives with behavioral descriptions.
CI guard (check_comment_hygiene.py) blocks reintroduced rot-prone refs via .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml, with EXCLUDED_FILES self-exclusion to isolate test fixtures.

Post-implementation tree scans revealed false-accept bug where path-embedded word-triple aliases incorrectly matched; fix required tightening alias pattern to reject file-path context while preserving sentence-final accepts.
